Unidata/MetPy.title: BUG: UDUnits-style powers must not be followed by a letter
Unidata/MetPy.body:
<!--
Thanks for contributing a pull request! Please ensure you have taken a look at
the contribution guidelines: https://github.com/Unidata/MetPy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

#### Description Of Changes

Change the regex transforming the UDUnits-style power specification (sticking the power right after the unit with no spaces) to pint-style units so that it doesn't also change chemical species: the change requires the factors be separated by spaces.  That is, 'm2 s-2' is fine (`m**2 s**-2`), 'm2s-2' is not (`m2s**-2`; `m2s` is not found in the registry).

I think most places strongly discourage the second.

Unidata/MetPy.title: Find peaks
Unidata/MetPy.body:
<!--
Thanks for contributing a pull request! Please ensure you have taken a look at
the contribution guidelines: https://github.com/Unidata/MetPy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

#### Description Of Changes

This adds `find_peaks` (and `persistence`) as API's for finding peaks, as well as makes `scattertext()` a public API for plotting this information. This is an alternative to #3110 that makes use of persistent homology as the mathematical underpinning for peak-finding in 2D. This runs in 30s on my mac for a 1377x2145 HRRR grid, which isn't too bad. It's much better for smaller grids.

TODO:
* [x] Improve example
* [x] Clean up `scattertext()`  a bit to handle formatting and broadcasting values 

In the meanwhile I wanted to get this up if anyone had API thoughts. Here's a quick example:
```python
import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import cartopy.feature as cfeature
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import metpy.calc as mpcalc
from metpy.cbook import get_test_data
import metpy.plots as mpplots
from metpy.units import units
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

data = xr.open_dataset(get_test_data('GFS_test.nc', as_file_obj=False)).metpy.parse_cf()
mslp = data.Geopotential_height_isobaric.metpy.sel(vertical=850*units.hPa).squeeze()
dataproj = mslp.metpy.cartopy_crs

h_y, h_x = mpcalc.find_peaks(mslp.values)
l_y, l_x = mpcalc.find_peaks(mslp.values, maxima=False)

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(8., 8.))
ax = fig.add_subplot(1, 1, 1, projection=ccrs.LambertConformal(central_longitude=-95))

clevmslp = np.arange(0., 2000., 30)
ax.contour(mslp.metpy.x, mslp.metpy.y, mslp,
           clevmslp, colors='k', linewidths=1.25, linestyles='solid', transform=dataproj)

mpplots.scattertext(ax, mslp.metpy.x[h_x], mslp.metpy.y[h_y], ['H']*2, size=20, color='red',
                    fontweight='bold', transform=dataproj)
mpplots.scattertext(ax, mslp.metpy.x[l_x], mslp.metpy.y[l_y], ['L']*4, size=20, color='blue',
                    fontweight='bold', transform=dataproj)
mpplots.scattertext(ax, mslp.metpy.x[l_x], mslp.metpy.y[l_y], [format(f, '.0f') for f in mslp.values[l_y, l_x]],
                    size=12, color='blue', fontweight='bold', loc=(0, -15), transform=dataproj)

ax.add_feature(cfeature.OCEAN)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAND)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.COASTLINE)
```

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2dd2e6f4-b765-41bf-839a-87c2ca22e214)

Unidata/MetPy.title: Ambaum 2020 saturation vapor pressure + phase handling
Unidata/MetPy.body:
**Dependent on #3725.**

In a Christmas Eve sprint, I implemented the analytic saturation vapor pressure from Ambaum 2020, per recommendations from #626. Lots of updated test values, and these may change further, but I wanted to get the changes out there quickly so we could evaluate their impacts, as well as get the changes into the full test matrix.

All departures are small in relative magnitude, but some callouts for potential scrutiny:
* `test_lfc_ml`
* `test_el` and its extensions
* any test involving cape_cin (mentioned in issue above as impacted, and needs LCL changes to see full picture.)
* `test_dewpoint_specific_humidity_xarray` (I reduced the precision instead of redefining the test data)

~~`test_equivalent_potential_temperature_masked` worked before. The calculations work on the individual masked array elements but for some reason it blows up on the full array. `numpy.ma.exp` offered no help. If anyone has any insight here it had me pulling my hair out a bit.~~ Marked this test, not the first time we've run into it in other contexts.

~~I'm not touching image tests until the other PR goes in and we tackle a review here, and maybe not even until LCL.~~ Done.

To support LCL validation and future support of automatic LCL/LDL/LFL handling, I've built on (and credited) some previous work to enhance certain moisture calcs to support `phase` handling. In this case, `saturation_vapor_pressure` now supports water vapor equilibrium partial pressure over liquid and ice, and can `auto`matically do so across the triple point temperature. I've plumbed this into moisture quantity calculations that depend on saturation vapor pressure as well.

I plan to follow up these changes with some tutorial and cookbook content in late Spring or early Summer.

Happy holidays! 🎅

Unidata/MetPy.title: Prevent frontogenesis from returning nans
Unidata/MetPy.body:
#### Description Of Changes

Previously, frontogenesis could return nans when there was a constant theta field (division by zero would occur) or if round-off error resulted in the argument to arcsin being slightly outside the valid domain of the function (-1 to 1).  In this commit, edits are made to set points to zero where nans occur due to division by zero (the frontogenesis is zero when the magnitude of the theta gradient is zero anyway) and to use np.clip to ensure the argument to arcsin is valid.

I could not come up with a simplified test case that triggers the round-off error issue with arcsin, but I do include a test case for the constant theta situation.  Because the test case results in a division by zero by design, it is currently failing since that triggers a RuntimeWarning.

<!--
Thanks for contributing a pull request! Please ensure you have taken a look at

#### Description Of Changes

Two new classes, named `Stuve` and `Emagram`, are constructed as child classes of the `SkewT` parent class.  They create Stüve diagrams and Emagrams, respectively. As child classes, they inherit plotting capabilities from SkewT (e.g. data, wind barbs, dry and saturated adiabats, and mixing ratio lines).

I confirmed that [Advanced Sounding example](https://unidata.github.io/MetPy/latest/examples/Advanced_Sounding.html) works with the new `Stuve` and and `Emagram` classes as drop-in replacements for `SkewT`.

This Closes #837 and addresses the Stuve request in #418.

#### Description Of Changes
This works around an issue where some ERA5 data had lat/lon with a "positive" attribute that, according to the CF specification, should indicate a vertical coordinate. Having lat be y and lon be x is already handled by a later block.

Unidata/MetPy.title: Standardize RH calcs on WMO8
Unidata/MetPy.body:
Standardize RH calculations on [WMO8](https://library.wmo.int/viewer/41650/download?file=8_I_2021_en.pdf&type=pdf&navigator=1) definition of relative humidity as

$$ RH = \frac{e}{e_s} $$

(eq 4.A.15)

such that any RH calculation with input of mixing ratio is made consistent with above as

$$ RH = \frac{w}{w_s} \frac{\epsilon + w_s}{\epsilon + w} $$

(eq 4.A.16)

As part of this process, we can also simplify `dewpoint_from_specific_humidity` to not require a temperature input. I've tried to do this in a way that allows arg and/or kwarg specification in a backwards compatible way. @dopplershift let me know your thoughts on the verbage here and how to best document this change and alert to an eventual deprecation. This does break our "check for versionchanged 1.0 and provide helpful error" handling in `_check_units_inner_helper`. ~I'm glad to change/remove that test or look into changing that handling.~ Handling slightly generalized and now issue a relatively quiet `PendingDeprecationWarning`.

~I've yet to update the test values so folks can see how much changed.~ **A few existing tests pass within tolerance but do have slightly changed values.**

#### Description Of Changes

<!--

request is merged. See https://github.com/blog/1506-closing-issues-via-pull-requests
-->

#### Checklist

- [x] Closes #3099
- [x] Tests added
- [ ] Fully documented


The [Canadian HRDPS model](https://eccc-msc.github.io/open-data/msc-data/nwp_hrdps/readme_hrdps-datamart_en/) is on a rotated latitude/longitude projection grid. This PR adds the capability for MetPy to parse its projection.

Minimal working example with HRDPS data:

```python
import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pyproj import CRS
import pygrib
import cfgrib
import xarray as xr
import sys
import metpy

# First, you should download a HRDPS grib2 file from
# https://dd.weather.gc.ca/model_hrdps/continental/2.5km/00/00/
# I grabbed the TMP_AGL-2m file...
FILE = "20230722T00Z_MSC_HRDPS_TMP_AGL-2m_RLatLon0.0225_PT000H.grib2"
ds = xr.open_dataset(FILE)

# Parse the projparams with pygrib, because cfgrib doesn't do this for you
# (see https://github.com/ecmwf/cfgrib/issues/251)
with pygrib.open(str(FILE)) as grb:
    msg = grb.message(1)
    cf_params = CRS(msg.projparams).to_cf()

ds["gribfile_projection"] = None
ds["gribfile_projection"].attrs = cf_params
for var in list(ds):
    if var == "gribfile_projection":
        continue
    ds[var].attrs["grid_mapping"] = "gribfile_projection"

# Ok, now we are ready to check that the changes to metpy/mapping.py worked...
variables = [i for i in list(ds) if len(ds[i].dims) > 0]
ds = ds.metpy.parse_cf(varname=variables)
crs = ds.metpy_crs.item().to_cartopy()

# And plot the data...
ax = plt.subplot(111, projection=crs)
ax.coastlines()
ax.pcolormesh(ds.longitude, ds.latitude, ds.t2m, transform=ccrs.PlateCarree())
ax.set_global()
ax.gridlines()
```

Unidata/MetPy.title: Adjust user-provided parcel temperature profile for NaN values in EL and LFC
Unidata/MetPy.body:
EL and LFC are functions that take a pressure profile, temperature profile, dewpoint profile, and an optional parcel temperature profile. When a missing value (np.NaN) is found in any of the profiles, the data point is removed, along with the data point at that level in _all_ the other profiles as well.

A bug described in #2921 shows that a missing value in any of the ambient profiles did not lead to the removal of a data point in the optional parcel temperature profile (when the user chose to provide that optional profile).

This PR introduces some rearrangements to the EL and LFC calculations to resolve that issue. Four new tests for NaN values in these calculations are also added.

The problem is that the original GEMPAK CED and MCD ([modified] cylindrical equidistant) projections, while supported by PROJ, aren't defined in the CF metadata spec (as of 1.10). Provided a path to a file, or a file-like object, the function returns a geopandas GeoDataFrame containing the data from the bulletin. pySTEPS/pysteps.title: Allow for possibility to end with full NWP weight at end of blending
pySTEPS/pysteps.body: This PR fixes #481. I have added a first, draft, approach to move to full NWP weights at the end of `timesteps`, if requested by the user. The method adds an additional input parameter for the `steps.blending.forecast` function: `timestep_start_full_nwp_weight: int, optional`: _The timestep, which should be smaller than timesteps, at which a linear transition takes place from the calculated weights to full NWP weight (and zero extrapolation and noise weight) to ensure the blending procedure becomes equal to the NWP forecast(s) at the last timestep of the blending procedure. If not provided, the blending stick to the theoretical weights provided by the chosen weights_method for a given lead time and skill of each blending component._ If a value is set for `timestep_start_full_nwp_weight`, the blending weights will linearly move from the weights at timestep `timestep_start_full_nwp_weight` to full weight (1.0) for the NWP component and zero (0.0) weight for the extrapolation and noise cascade components at the final timestep of the blending procedure. I have given it a first test with the gallery example data from Australia. We only have three hours of NWP sample data here, so `timestep_start_full_nwp_weight` is set at 12 (2 hour lead time) and `timesteps` is set at 18 (3 hours in total). Testing this with the BPS weights, give the following weights with (a) indicating the current setup and (b) indicating the setup where `timestep_start_full_nwp_weight` is applied: ![Blending_weights_BPS](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21144ba0-5378-4a59-b129-6762276b5760) The forecast will then change from: [original] to: [adjusted] ![Forecast_BPS_adjusted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09af9693-397b-4dd0-aec6-0665e72d4cda)

ARM-DOE/pyart.title: FIX/ENH: vad_michelson skips missing gates (#1488) and rejects unreliable fits
ARM-DOE/pyart.body:
## PR tags (required)

- [x] scientific/algorithmic
- [x] design/architecture (two new options)

## What changed
- **Fix:** `vad_michelson` skips missing gates. Before, it counted them, so wind speeds came out too low.
- **Fix:** results no longer depend on the operating system when gate heights tie.
- **Enhancement:** each gate is now fitted by least squares (`v = c + a sin(az) + b cos(az)`), and the fit reports its own speed error.
  - `max_speed_error` (default 2 m/s) drops gates whose fit is unreliable: too few rays, rays bunched in one part of the circle, or noisy data.
  - Height bins are averaged weighted by 1/error², and a dropped gate no longer blanks the whole bin.
  - `valid_ray_min` (default 16, same as `vad_browning`) is a simple extra guard.
- Five new tests, a gallery example (`examples/retrieve/plot_vad_michelson.py`), and a Notes section in the docstring.

`vad_browning` is unchanged. It could share the same fit in a follow-up.

## Why
The more gates were missing, the lower the wind: 30% missing gave speeds about 30% too low (#1488). Fixing that exposed spikes that the low bias had been hiding. On the #1488 case, one height jumped to 110 kt against 41 kt from Level 3. The error-based fit removes them.

On the #1488 case, compared with the NEXRAD Level 3 wind profile:

![KEOX vs Level 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgrover1/pyart/assets/vad-1488/vad_1488_keox_l3_v3.png)

| | Bias | Average error |
|-|-|-|
| Before | 36 kt too slow | 36 kt |
| After | 4 kt too fast | 6 kt |
| `vad_browning` | 5 kt too fast | 6 kt |

More cases: [profiles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgrover1/pyart/assets/vad-1488/vad_1488_profiles_v4.png). On KLIX the two methods agree. On KLBB (weak echo, light winds) this fit reads 2–4 m/s faster than `vad_browning`. `vad_browning` reads low when rays cover only part of the circle (4.5 instead of 5.0 m/s with a 120° gap in a synthetic test). Against the nearest soundings (Amarillo and Midland, 12Z and 00Z), this fit is closer: bias −1.1 m/s against −3.7 m/s for `vad_browning`.

![KLBB vs soundings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgrover1/pyart/assets/vad-1488/vad_1488_klbb_soundings.png)

[Scripts](https://github.com/mgrover1/pyart/tree/assets/vad-1488).

## Issues closed
Closes #1488

## Target version
- [x] next minor

## Validation
- [x] I ran pre-commit or ruff: clean
- [x] I ran tests: full suite passes locally (849 passed). Each new test failed before its change.

## AI usage & manual verification
- AI used: yes
- Model/tooling: Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context, `claude-opus-5-5`)
- Tasks delegated to AI: diagnosis, fix, tests, figures
- Manual verification performed: reviewed the diff and figures

## Manual verification
- [x] Compared before and after: speeds go up wherever gates are missing, and the spikes are gone. With no missing gates, results change by less than 0.1 m/s.
- [x] Checked against a known baseline: the NEXRAD Level 3 product (above) and synthetic winds of known speed.
- [x] Backward compatibility: two new optional arguments. Existing calls still work, but results change.

ARM-DOE/pyart.title: FIX: Scale ODIM rstart by declared version (metres since ODIM_H5 2.4)
ARM-DOE/pyart.body:
## PR tags (required)
Select all that apply.

- [ ] docs-only
- [ ] tests-only
- [x] tiny-change (<5 lines of code in 1 or 2 files)
- [ ] big refactor
- [x] scientific/algorithmic
- [ ] design/architecture

## What changed
- `read_odim_h5` now reads the ODIM version from the `Conventions` attribute (`ODIM_H5/Vx_y`) before it converts `rstart`.
- Files from version 2.4 onward: `rstart` is already in metres, so no conversion happens. Older files, or files with no readable version: keep the existing km → m conversion.
- `meters_to_center_of_first_gate` uses the same corrected value.
- Adds `tests/aux_io/test_odim_h5.py`, with small synthetic ODIM files built with h5py, so no new data files.

## Why
ODIM_H5 2.4 switched `rstart` to metres. Py-ART multiplied it by 1000 anyway, so for 2.4 files with a non-zero `rstart`, the whole range array moved about 1000× too far out, with no warning.

## Issues closed
Closes #1869

ARM-DOE/pyart.title: FIX: xradar accessor compatibility — coercion helper, Radar parity, masked fields, RHI support
ARM-DOE/pyart.body:
Continues roadmap Highest-Priority #3 (xarray/xradar integration). Closes #1765.

- Adds public `pyart.xradar.to_pyart_radar()` and uses it in `correct.bias_and_noise`, so `calc_cloud_mask`/`calc_noise_floor`/`range_correction`/`calc_zdr_offset` accept xradar DataTrees and `Xradar` objects. **API note:** invalid `radar` arguments to these functions now raise `TypeError` (was `ValueError`).
- Fixes #1765: moments named `z`/`x`/`y` (e.g. GAMIC reflectivity) are no longer shadowed or dropped by georeference coordinates.
- Adds missing `Radar` parity members on `Xradar`: `get_elevation`, `get_gate_area`, `info`, `rays_per_sweep`/`init_rays_per_sweep`, `init_gate_altitude` alias (the roadmap names `radar.info` explicitly).
- Optional platform/scan attributes (`scan_rate`, `rotation`, `tilt`, `antenna_transition`, `radar_calibration`, etc.) are now looked up in the DataTree when present instead of hardcoded `None`/`AttributeError`; `None` when absent, never fabricated.
- `Xradar` fields are now `np.ma.MaskedArray` (NaN-masked), matching `Radar` and fixing `despeckle_field` and other mask-dependent algorithms.
- RHI scans no longer collapse to one ray per sweep in `_combine_sweeps` and `add_field` (dedup key follows scan type); collision-path georeferencing is cached.
- `Xgrid` gains `projection_proj` and `write`.

Known limitation (pre-existing, not addressed here): some real RHI files (e.g. DOW8 samples in open_radar_data) still fail in `_combine_sweeps` via a separate dimension-mismatch path; follow-up issue to come.

Tests: `tests/xradar/test_accessor.py` + `tests/correct/test_correct_bias.py` = 34 passed. A companion test-matrix PR (stacked on this one) adds a Radar-vs-Xradar equality suite.

ARM-DOE/pyart.title: ADD: Create CAPPI from Radar
ARM-DOE/pyart.body:
<!-- Please remove check-list items that aren't relevant to your changes -->

- [x] Closes #597 #1639 #985 #980 #1585
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Documentation reflects changes   ---  Not sure

#### Description:
This PR introduces a new feature to generate a Constant Altitude Plan Position Indicator (CAPPI) from radar data directly within Py-ART. The new `create_cappi` function allows users to specify the altitude and radar fields for CAPPI generation, simplifying the process and making it more accessible.

The implementation draws on existing work, with valuable insights from the `comp_z.py` module by @dopplerchase and @vlouf's [CAPPI notebook](https://github.com/vlouf/radar_cappi/blob/master/CAPPI.ipynb). This addition integrates and builds on these concepts, providing a streamlined way to create CAPPI products within Py-ART.

#### Example Usage:

```python
import pyart
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from open_radar_data import DATASETS

# Load the sample radar data
file = DATASETS.fetch("RAW_NA_000_125_20080411190016")
radar = pyart.io.read(file)

# Create CAPPI at 2,000 meters and 10,000 meters for the 'reflectivity' field
cappi_2k = pyart.retrieve.create_cappi(radar, fields=['reflectivity'], height=2000)
cappi_10k = pyart.retrieve.create_cappi(radar, fields=['reflectivity'], height=10_000)

# Display the CAPPI at both altitudes
cappi2k_display = pyart.graph.RadarMapDisplay(cappi_2k)
cappi10k_display = pyart.graph.RadarMapDisplay(cappi_10k)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))
cappi2k_display.plot_ppi('reflectivity', vmin=-10, vmax=60, ax=ax[0])
cappi10k_display.plot_ppi('reflectivity', vmin=-10, vmax=60, ax=ax[1])
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6e913b5-0cb5-4dd3-ae77-17983f193d35)

This function leverages existing capabilities in Py-ART to offer a consistent and user-friendly method for generating CAPPI visualizations, making it a valuable addition to the toolkit.

pytroll/satpy.title: Check optional datasets in NIREmissivePartFromReflectance
pytroll/satpy.body:
- [x] Closes #2460
 - [x] Tests added
 - [x] Fully documented
 - [x] Add your name to `AUTHORS.md` if not there already

`NIRReflectance.__call__` passes `projectables + optional_datasets` to `match_data_arrays`, but `NIREmissivePartFromReflectance.__call__` passes only `projectables`. Both classes read the optional datasets in the shared `_get_nir_inputs`, for the sun zenith angle and for the 13.4µm brightness temperature, so in the subclass a mismatched optional skips the geometry check entirely and reaches pyspectral unvalidated.

That is the bug behind #2460. @djhoese identified the cause in the thread in December 2023:

> Ooohhh `optional_datasets` isn't included in the projectables but it should be. That's the "proper" fix for this I think. [...] In that case `match_data_arrays` would have raised `IncompatibleAreas` and the "derive" function never would have been called.

The parent class was fixed. The subclass was not, and still reproduces the original report on current `main`. With a full-resolution NIR channel and a half-resolution sun zenith angle:

```
NIRReflectance                   -> IncompatibleAreas (correct, caught before compute)
NIREmissivePartFromReflectance   -> ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together
                                    with shapes (1200, 1500) (2400, 3000)
```

**The quieter failure matters more.** A shape mismatch at least fails loudly. An optional dataset with a *matching* shape but a different area broadcasts fine, so nothing raises at all and the emissive part is derived from a sun zenith angle belonging to a different place:

| optional dataset | `NIRReflectance` | `NIREmissivePartFromReflectance` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same shape, different area | `IncompatibleAreas` | **no exception** |
| no `area` attribute | `ValueError: Missing 'area' attribute` | **no exception** |

Both rows raise after this change.

### The change

Rather than copying the matching line into the subclass, this moves it into a shared `_match_projectables_and_optionals` helper on `NIRReflectance` that both `__call__`s use. Copying was how the two diverged in the first place; a shared helper makes divergence structurally impossible for this pair. Happy to collapse it back to a mirrored line if you would rather keep the diff minimal.

Nothing public changes. `match_data_arrays` remains the overridable seam, so a third-party subclass overriding it still gets its override invoked through the helper.

**A second, smaller bug came along with it.** Both classes advertise `optional_datasets=None` in their signature, and both crash on `main` if you actually pass it:

```
NIRReflectance                   -> TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "NoneType") to list
NIREmissivePartFromReflectance   -> TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable
```

The `optional_datasets or []` in the helper handles both. Nothing in `Scene._generate_composite` passes `None` today, since `_get_prereq_datasets` always returns a list, so this only affects direct callers. Say the word if you would rather see it separately.

### Testing

Five tests, each parametrized over both classes, covering: differing resolutions on the sun zenith optional, differing resolutions on the 13.4µm optional, a same-shape/different-area optional, an optional with no `area`, and no optionals at all.

I mutation tested these rather than trusting a green run. Reverting the subclass to the original line fails five of them. Checking only the sun-zenith optional and skipping the CO2 one fails exactly the two CO2 parameters, which is why that test exists rather than being redundant. Dropping the `None` guard fails the no-optionals parameters. Crossing the two returned slices fails six pre-existing tests.

**One mutation my tests do not kill**, stated rather than papered over: running the check and then passing the *unmatched* arrays on to `_get_nir_inputs` passes everything. I looked for an honest assertion that would catch it and could not find one. Only `.data` is ever read from an optional, so `drop_coordinates` and `align_geo_coordinates` cannot reach the output, and dask unifies chunks during blockwise regardless, which I confirmed by chunking the sun zenith angle differently from the NIR channel and getting identical result chunks either way. For the optionals it looks like an equivalent mutant. A chunk assertion would pass for the wrong reason, so I left it out.

Two intentional behaviour changes in the subclass worth flagging. Chunk unification now spans the optionals as well as the projectables, so output chunking can be a finer common refinement than before; values are unchanged and this matches what the parent already did. And an optional lacking an `area` now raises `ValueError` rather than being ignored, which `Scene._generate_composite` does not catch the way it catches `IncompatibleAreas`. Both are existing parent-class semantics now extended to the subclass, and there is a test pinning the second one.

I checked that no configuration relies on a mismatched optional. In `visir.yaml`, `nir_reflectance` and `nir_emissive` have identical prerequisites and optional prerequisites and differ only in the class, and `viirs.yaml` deliberately pins the sun zenith resolution to the band (`M15` with 742, `I05` with 371). So there is no config in which the subclass receives an optional set the parent does not also receive under the same geometry, which means anything that would newly raise here would already be raising in the parent today.

`376 passed, 2 xfailed` across `satpy/tests/test_modifiers.py`, `satpy/tests/modifier_tests/` and `satpy/tests/compositor_tests/`, clean under `-W error`, ruff clean.

pytroll/satpy.title: Fix required NetCDF root variable collection
pytroll/satpy.body:
Fixes #2704.

`_collect_listed_variables` currently relies on the loop variable `p` after iterating over path components. For a root variable that loop does not execute, which raises `UnboundLocalError`. A root variable following an attribute can also inherit the previous `p == "attr"` state and be skipped.

This replaces that implicit loop-variable state with an explicit per-item attribute flag, preserving existing grouped-variable and attribute handling while allowing root variables to be collected correctly.

Regression coverage includes:
- a required root variable with no `/` in its name
- a root variable immediately following a required attribute

pytroll/satpy.title: Cleanup up composite utility 'add_bands' function
pytroll/satpy.body:
See the conversation in #3333 (CC @SalimMessaad1). The summary is that the `add_bands` utility function in `satpy.composites.core` is a little confusing to follow. Mostly, it isn't clear due to the lack of documentation what the second argument should be. If we look at the actual uses of it in Satpy the second argument should always be `some_data_arr.coords["bands"]`. However, there was a `bands = bands.compute()` call to work around a dask bug so it kind of seemed like it should be a regular image data `DataArray` that is passed. But I don't think a "bands" coordinate has any reason to ever be a dask array (versus a numpy array) so I'm not sure why this was ever needed. Additionally, all the tests (either added by @mraspaud or @pnuu, or maybe just refactored to the current location :man_shrugging: ) always pass a `DataArray` where the bands information is in the `.data` part, not just the `.coords["bands"]`. This is never the way this function is used in Satpy.

So this PR:

* Adds docstring information
* Adds type annotations
* Allows "bands" (the second argument) to be a Sequenced (ex. list) or a DataArray and describes in the docstring that the DataArray should come from `.coords["bands"]` of an image array.
* Remove the dask workaround of `bands = bands.compute()` as it is from a 2020 bug and never should have been needed(?)
* Tests have been parametrized
* Tests now properly use the `.coords["bands"]` for the bands argument
* Tests enforce no dask computation
* Fix other various mypy issues (mostly satpy.composites.viirs)

Remaining question for (@mraspaud @gerritholl @pnuu):

The tests use 32-bit float input and make sure it remains 32-bit float data. I think this is reasonable as the actual use cases in Satpy are all with pre-enhanced data I think. So everything is normalized to 0-1 floating point numbers except for maybe some edge cases with integers. In the cases where an Alpha band is added it is set to all 1s. Do we want to support the case of integers where alpha is set to max-int for that integer type? Or maybe we just fail for now and handle/update the code when someone has a legitimate use case for that?

pytroll/satpy.body:
When reading FCI L1c data, the attributes of the loaded datasets are modified to 1) include some additional metadata taken from other parts of the file and 2) avoid unwanted attributes that are not relevant to the calibrated data but may have been propagated to the final dataset, depending on xarray's policy regarding attribute propagation.

With this PR, the procedure of handling those attributes is moved outside of the `_get_dataset_measurand` method (which loads and calibrate the data) and into a new `_set_and_cleanup_attributes` method (addressing issue #3286). It also introduces a check for unwanted `_FillValue` which did not exist before, solving #3284.

In addition to refactoring, this new method is also called by the other three dataset loader methods `_get_dataset_quality`, `_get_dataset_index_map`, and `_get_dataset_aux_data`, so all loaded datasets inherit e.g. the `time_parameters` dictionary attribute. 


 - [x] Closes #3284 and #3286 
 - [x] Tests added: add the `vis_06` channel test to `test_drop_fill_value` test
 - [x] Fully documented (as a docstring to the new method)

This PR fixes the issue, falling back to the `i` stripe grid if the `f` stripe is not present.

In addition, I add S3C and S3D to the list of platforms in preparation for their launches in the coming years. I also update the link to the product notice.

pytroll/satpy.title: Fix inconsistent docstring of correction limit in sunz modifiers
pytroll/satpy.body:
<!-- Describe what your PR does, and why -->
This PR fixes inconsistent documentation for the `correction_limit` argument in the `__init__` docstrings of the `SunZenithCorrector` and `EffectiveSolarPathlengthCorrector` classes.

Previously:
- The **class-level docstrings** correctly explained that beyond `correction_limit` the correction is *gradually reduced to 0 at* `max_sza`, and is *constant only if* `max_sza=None`.
- The **`__init__` docstrings**, however, stated that the correction was always constant beyond `correction_limit`, which contradicted the actual behavior.

This PR updates the `__init__` docstrings to match the class-level explanation, ensuring clarity and avoiding confusion for users (especially those reading docstrings via IDEs or `help()`).

pytroll/satpy.body:
<!-- Describe what your PR does, and why -->
This is an attempt to fix #3167 . For datasets with multiple timesteps, compute time bounds based on time coordinates, except for the last timestep where `end_time` from dataset attributes is used. Example with 3 timesteps (`t` is the time coordinate)

```
[
    (t[0], t[1]),
    (t[1], t[2]),
    (t[2], min. end time from dataset attributes)
]
```

For datasets with a single timestep, the bounds remain unchanged

```
[
    (min. start time from dataset attributes, min. end time from dataset attributes)
]
```

I'm a bit confused about the usage of minimum for the end time here. I would have expected the maximum end time. Maybe someone has a clue?

@ameraner  when we provide only one file the `combine_metadata` returns the content of the attributes directly as stated [here](https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/blob/main/satpy/dataset/metadata.py#L69-L71). In the other case the attributes of each files are compared between each other. As the coefficient `radiance_unit_conversion_coefficient` is a xarray.dataArray the comparison is done into this [function](https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/blob/main/satpy/dataset/metadata.py#L197-L204). According to this line  `if hasattr(arrays[0], "compute")` is considered as lazy array which is false in our case because it is a non daskified array. 

So I have change the criteria to check if it is a lazy array to `if isinstance(arrays[0].data, da.Array)`

pytroll/satpy.title: Add a reader for NWC SAF GEO HRW data
pytroll/satpy.body:
This PR adds a reader for the High Resolution Winds data from NWC SAF GEO.

The data structure is very complex, and due to the unsupported compound data type can't be opened with `xr.open_dataset()`. Because there are 259 datasets, I've made the dataset definitions dynamic instead of putting them into the reader YAML. The code is in a separate file because the internal structure is completely different to the other NWC SAF GEO products (see the linked issue).

By default the file handler reads the datasets separately for each imaging channel. That is, the datasets are named `wind_vis06_air_pressure`, `wind_hrvis_wind_speed`, and so on. The prefix is the name of the channel within the files.

The user can also supply `reader_kwargs={"merge_channels": True}` to collect all the data together. In this case the datasets are named without the prefix, such as `air_pressure`, `wind_speed`, etc.

pytroll/satpy.title: Fix seviri_l2_grib end_time property bug.
pytroll/satpy.body:
<!-- Describe what your PR does, and why -->
As described in #2942, the changes in https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/pull/2717 lead to the `end_time` property not working for SEVIRI data, since we now use the sub-satellite point to determine the scanning mode and thus the temporal resolution used to determine the `end_time` from the `start_time` (prior to https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/pull/2717 it was always set to 15 minutes, which is incorrect for RSS data). However, the `self._ssp_lon` attribute is only available after a dataset and its metadata have been loaded and thus an `AttributeError` was raised during `Scene` initialization. This was not covered by the unit test and a human error lead to the bug being unnoticed also when testing with real data.

This PR adapts the `end_time` property to return `None` if no dataset has been loaded, meaning that `_ssp_lon` is not available. As soon as a dataset has been loaded, both `scn.end_time` and `scn[dataset].attrs['end_time']` will have valid and correct `datetime.datetime` objects. The unit test has been adapted to cover this bug.

 - [X] Closes #2942 
 - [X] Tests adapted to capture this bug

pytroll/satpy.title: Update pyhdf-based arrs to be manually tokenized
pytroll/satpy.body:
This avoids a bug in dask or cloudpickle that alters the state of the pyhdf SDS object in some way making it unusable. The PR in dask that started triggering this was in https://github.com/dask/dask/pull/11320. My guess is that the repeated pickling/serialization is losing some hidden state in the pyhdf SDS object and then pyhdf or HDF-C no longer knows how to work with it.

We could register SDS with normalize_token in dask or we could just do what I do in this PR and come up with the token/name ourselves. Note this is the name for the dask array/task. This is similar to work done in the past by @mraspaud for the HDF5 utility package to make sure things are consistent across file variable loads.

One alternative to the PR as it is right now would be to copy `from_sds` as a method on the HDF utility class so it knows how to use `self.filename` automatically for the tokenizing. Also I'm realizing maybe the src_path shouldn't be required as it is only used if the `name` kwarg isn't provided. Thoughts @mraspaud @gerritholl ?

pytroll/satpy.title: Fix AGRI L1 C07 having a valid LUT value for its fill value
pytroll/satpy.body:
Closes https://github.com/ssec/polar2grid/issues/565

CC @simonrp84 

This was first encountered in Geo2Grid development by @kathys. Some debugging showed that C07 files for AGRI L1 have a LUT with 65536 elements in it even though 65535 is a fill value. The end result is fill values being replaced by real BT values.

This PR implements one possible solution. It says "if the LUT already includes the fill value, force that LUT value to NaN". An alternative could be slicing the LUT array to the input data's `valid_range` and then getting NaN for anything beyond the LUT. The ending implementation ends up looking pretty similar I think.

Note: I haven't added tests for this yet because I wanted to give @simonrp84 time to review the solution as soon as possible. I also wanted to see if this would work without having to (likely) rewrite a ton of the tests to fit the situation...which is basically a bug in the input data.

pytroll/satpy.title: Anticipate filehandler sorting in `GEOSegmentYAMLReader` to have sorted handlers also with `pad_data=False`
pytroll/satpy.body:
This PR fixes the issue reported in https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/issues/2588 by making the segment sorting happen early during `create_filehandlers`, so that it acts for both `pad_data=True` and `False`. 

The root cause was that the filehandler sorting _by segment_ was done only in the default `pad_data=True` branch inside the padding mechanism of `GEOSegmentYAMLReader`. When calling e.g. `scn.load(['ir_105'], pad_data=False, upper_right_corner='NE')`, in the previous implementation the filehandlers were being sorted (in the base `FileYAMLReader.create_filehandlers`) only by `start_time` (which is always the same after https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/pull/2420), and then alphabetically by filenames. This is problematic for FCI where sorting alphabetically means sorting by `processing_time`, and there are cases where the `processing_time` order does not correspond to the chunk order (due to parallel processing), causing the issue. 

Note that even without https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/pull/2420, some FCI segments have the same filename `start_time`, hence the bug would have happened anyway.

pytroll/satpy.title: Fix composites failing on non-aligned geolocation coordinates
pytroll/satpy.body:
See #2668 for detailed discussion. Basically #2610 switched from the internal satpy base resampler to the pyresample base resampler class. This overall isn't a problem except for the pyresample base resample has a shortcut where it won't process an input if it detects that the target geometry is the same as the source geometry. In those cases it returns the original DataArray with no additional modification. This logically/theoretically shouldn't be a problem, but it reveals a larger issue.

When y and x coordinates are generated from different sources they may have very small differences due to floating point precision issues. So example an x and y that are a subset/slice of a larger pair of x/y arrays may be different than an x/y generated from a sliced/subset AreaDefinition of the same original area definition (again, look at my comments in the referenced issue).

This PR updates one part of Satpy to make these operations work as overall the resampler change revealed an existing issue that was previously being hidden. The composite base class now performs a call to `xarray.align` to make sure that input arrays are compatible, but for `y` and `x` coordinates it will re-assign them to match the first input. The docstring in the new method explains any concerns about this.

pytroll/satpy.title: Fix geolocation errors of the FY-4 AGRI reader base
pytroll/satpy.body:
<!-- Describe what your PR does, and why -->
Fix the offset calculations in FY-4 reader base according to HSD reader.

 - [x] Closes #2532 <!-- remove if there is no corresponding issue, which should only be the case for minor changes -->
 - [x] Tests added <!-- for all bug fixes or enhancements -->

**1.Area extent of the GEOS projection**
This is calculated by column/line offset (COFF/LOFF), CFAC, width/height of the image using `get_area_extent` under `_geos_area`. But, this method begins at (0, 0) which is fit for full-disk image. When the scan mode is regional, the initial column/line position is also important. And that is why FY-4 REGC mode got the wrong area.

**2.Comparison between Himawari HSD with FY-4**
HSD reader, no matter whether the data is fulldisk / regional, also uses `get_area_extent` . The differences are:

**Himawari full-disk COFF/LOFF**
`[22000.5, 11000.5, 5500.5, 2750.5, 1375.5]`
**Himawari full-disk width/height**
`[44000, 22000, 11000, 5500, 2750]`

**FY-4 full-disk COFF/LOFF**
`[21983.5, 10991.5, 5495.5, 2747.5, 1373.5]`
**FY-4 full-disk width/height**
`[43968, 21984, 10992, 5496, 2748]`

Apparently,
`Himawari's offset = width(height) / 2 + 0.5`
While
`FY-4's offset = width(height) / 2 - 0.5`
That 1 pixel diff could explain why FY-4's center coord isn't at (0, 0).

And the calculation:
Himawari:
```
pdict['coff'] = np.float32(self.proj_info['COFF'])
pdict['loff'] = -np.float32(self.proj_info['LOFF']) + 1
pdict['loff'] = pdict['loff'] + (self.segment_number * pdict['nlines'])

pdict['ncols'] = width
pdict['nlines'] = height
```
When testing on a target-area scanning dataset `HS_H09_20230701_0000_B01_R301_R10_S0101.DAT`:
```
pdict['coff'] = 360.5
pdict['loff'] = -2279.5
```
The COFF/LOFF of HSD is stored inside the dataset, not fixed like FY-4. So it seems that these two numbers come from nowhere. But, if this regional image reprojected to full-disk frame, it is clear that the scanning start at **col 5140 / line 2220**.
![image](https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/assets/72339781/a7f39ca1-1fef-40be-93b4-3976a18b2000)
This is a 1000x1000 B01 dataset. The fulldisk size of B01 is 11000 and the COFF/LOFF is 5500.5.

Therefore:
```
pdict['coff'] = fulldisk_COFF - start_column
pdict['loff'] = -fulldisk_LOFF + 1 + start_line + pdict['nlines']
```

**3.Back on FY-4**
Because of the 1-pixel difference:
```
pdict['coff'] = fulldisk_COFF - start_column + 1
pdict['loff'] = -fulldisk_LOFF + 1 + start_line + pdict['nlines'] - 1 = -fulldisk_LOFF + start_line + pdict['nlines']
```
Further:
`end_line + 1 = start_line + pdict['nlines']`
```
pdict['coff'] = fulldisk_COFF - start_column + 1
pdict['loff'] = -fulldisk_LOFF + end_line + 1
```
Luckily, both `start_column` and `end_line` are attributes in the FY-4 HDF files. So it is very easy to get them.

4.Results
The center point back to zero.
![image](https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/assets/72339781/62c3e1bc-7149-4350-995e-940a40eaa46a)

And the REGC image
![image](https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/assets/72339781/6a87cdba-7ff4-45dc-873e-ea92f2facdad)

pytroll/satpy.title: Drop default compression in CF Writer
pytroll/satpy.body:
<!-- Describe what your PR does, and why -->

Drop default compression in CF Writer and delegate this to the user (via encoding keyword argument or dataset attribute). This closes #2244. Also, update documentation to use the new `compression` keyword instead of `zlib`, which closes #2386 .

I played around a bit with different combinations of backend versions (netCDF4, libnetcdf, xarray) and noticed that the keyword choice also depends on the underlying libnetcdf. If `libnetcdf<4.9.0` only `zlib` works and `compression` is silently ignored. This is the case in our CI environment where`eccodes` currently requires `libnetcdf-4.8`.

In order to make users aware of that, I added a little section in the documentation and issued a user warning if the backend versions don't match. 

Waiting for https://github.com/pytroll/satpy/pull/2391 to fix flake8 errors.

pytroll/satpy.body:

When defining a composite with a palettize enhancement where the palette is read from the source file, one **should not** set `min_value` and `max_value` in the enhancement configuration! pytroll/satpy.title: Fix ancillary variable confusion after resampling
pytroll/satpy.body:
Fix ancillary variable confusion after resampling.

Previously, `replace_anc()` was only looking at `_satpy_id_keys` in the variable attributes.  When this was not set, it would use `None` for constructing the `DataID`s used for comparison.  When we pass `None` as ID keys to `DataID`, the `DataID` becomes empty: `DataID()`, such that a comparison always evaluates to True.  As a consequence, instead of replacing the "correct" of N ancillary variables, it would replace the first one N times and the other ones not at all.

In this PR, I am taking the `default_id_keys_config` if no `_satpy_id_keys` are set in the variable attributes.

wradlib/wradlib.title: FIX: set z coordinate units to meters in georeference
wradlib/wradlib.body:
- [x] Closes #791
 - [x] Tests added
 - [x] Passes `black . && ruff check .`
 - [x] Fully documented (e.g. docstrings)

`georeference()` derived a single `unit` from the x-axis of the target CRS and applied it to both `z` and `gr`. Under a geographic CRS that labels `z` — a beam height in meters — as `degrees_east`, as reported in #791.

`z` is now always `meters`. It never depends on the target CRS: `spherical_to_xyz` always builds a 2-axis AEQD source, so PROJ passes `z` through untouched even for a compound CRS whose vertical axis is in feet (verified against EPSG:8712).

`gr` needed a different treatment rather than the same hardcoding. `misc.ground_range` computes a geodesic distance in meters for a geographic CRS, but a euclidean distance in *CRS units* for a projected one, so `gr` now follows the CRS except when geographic.

Same sweep through six CRSs, after the change:

| target CRS | `x` units | `gr` units | `gr.max` | `z.max` |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `None` (native AEQD) | `metre` | `metre` | 99480.3 | 1550.9 |
| EPSG:4326 (geographic 2D) | `degrees_east` | `meters` | 99480.3 | 1550.9 |
| EPSG:4979 (geographic 3D) | `degrees_east` | `meters` | 99480.3 | 1550.9 |
| EPSG:3857 (projected, m) | `metre` | `metre` | 122526.3 | 1550.9 |
| EPSG:3433 (projected, ftUS) | `0.3048006... metre` | `0.3048006... metre` | 326413.3 | 1550.9 |
| EPSG:8712 (compound, ftUS) | `0.3048006... metre` | `0.3048006... metre` | 326413.3 | 1550.9 |

Only the numeric metadata changes; no coordinate values are touched.

### Notes for reviewers

`meters` is used rather than pyproj's `metre` to match `xradar.model.get_altitude_attrs()` / `get_range_attrs()`, which `georef/misc.py` already uses for `bin_altitude` / `bin_distance`. This does change the AEQD default path for `z` from `metre` to `meters`. Happy to switch if you would rather keep the pyproj spelling, though it then disagrees with the neighbouring functions.

Two pre-existing issues in `misc.ground_range` surfaced while working on this, both left alone as out of scope — happy to open a separate issue:

1. The projected branch is a bare `sqrt(dx**2 + dy**2)` in CRS units, with the comment *"Assume CRS units are meters"*, while the docstring promises meters. That is why `gr` has to inherit the CRS units here instead of the function guaranteeing them.
2. For conformal projections that distance is not a ground range at all. The EPSG:3857 row above reads 122526 against 99480 everywhere else — Web Mercator's `sec(35°)` inflation — so the value is unit-correct but semantically wrong for a coordinate carrying `standard_name="distance_from_radar"`.

### Tests

`test_georeference_z_gr_units` is parametrized over AEQD, geographic and a US-survey-foot projected CRS. It fails on all three params against the current `main`.

`CoordinateTransformIndexingAdapter._oindex_get` did not drop axes indexed by an integer; only `__getitem__` squeezed them. pydata/xarray.title: Fix DataTree.load skipping variables whose name matches a group path
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

Fixes #11672.

`DataTree.load` builds a `lazy_data` dict of chunked variables keyed by **node path**, then after computing them walks the tree again and loads anything that was not already evaluated:

```python
# load everything else sequentially
for node in self.subtree:
    for k, v in node.variables.items():
        if k not in lazy_data:
            v.load()
```

The guard here compares a **variable name** `k` with `lazy_data`, whose keys are **group paths**. When a variable name happens to match any path in the tree, the variable is treated as already loaded and stays lazy.

The reporter's reproducer trips this on the first node:

```python
xr.DataTree.from_dict({"/a": xr.Dataset({"a": 0})}).to_netcdf("test.nc")
xr.load_datatree("test.nc").to_netcdf("test.nc")
# RuntimeError: NetCDF: Write to read only
# Raised while encoding variable 'a' with value <xarray.Variable ()>
```

`subtree_with_keys` yields `('.', root)` and `('a', group_a)`. The group's single variable is also named `a`, which is a key of `lazy_data`, so the second loop never calls `v.load()`. The write then tries to read it back from the file it's overwriting, and the netCDF driver aborts the save after it has already dropped the variable from the group.

The fix iterates with `subtree_with_keys` and checks membership against the inner dict for the current node, so only the variables actually evaluated by the chunked path are skipped:

```python
for path, node in self.subtree_with_keys:
    for k, v in node.variables.items():
        if k not in lazy_data[path]:
            v.load()
```

### Checklist

- [x] Closes #11672
- [x] Tests added
- [x] User visible changes (including notable bug fixes) are documented in `whats-new.rst`
- [ ] New functions/methods are listed in `api.rst`

### Tests

Added `test_load_datatree_overwrite_same_named_variable` in `NetCDFIOBase`, so the regression runs under all three netCDF variants (`TestNetCDF4DatatreeIO`, `TestH5NetCDFDatatreeIO`, `TestGenericNetCDFIO`). It covers both a root-level `/a` with variable `a` and a nested `/b/b` with variable `c` (to catch any path-encoding regressions in nested groups). All three fail on `main` with `NetCDF: Write to read only` / `KeyError: 'a'` and pass with the fix. Full `xarray/tests/backends/test_datatree.py` and `xarray/tests/test_datatree.py` suites pass locally (179 passed, 50 skipped from missing optional deps; 156 passed, 5 xfailed).

pydata/xarray.title: Fix assign_coords dropping pandas Series index name
pydata/xarray.body:
## Description

Fixes #9284. When assigning a pandas `Series` with a named index as a coordinate (e.g. `da.assign_coords(new_coord=series)`), `as_variable()` ignored the Series' own index name and used the `assign_coords` keyword as the dimension instead, causing a confusing `CoordinateValidationError`.

## Root cause

In `as_variable()` (xarray/core/variable.py), a `pd.Index` with a name is already special-cased to use its own name as the dimension. A plain `pd.Series` had no such special case, so it fell through to the generic branch that uses the keyword/dict key as the dimension name, discarding the Series' index name entirely.

## Fix

When a `pd.Series` has a named index, convert it to a `DataArray` first (which already handles pandas objects correctly), so the index name is preserved as the dimension. A Series with an unnamed index still falls back to the keyword name, as before (verified with a regression test).

Dataset.interp with assume_sorted=False called sortby on all interpolated dimensions, which indexes with an integer array and copies the data even when the coordinate is already increasing. Now increasing coordinates and dimensions without a coordinate are left alone, strictly decreasing coordinates are reversed with a slice, and only the remaining dimensions go through sortby.

Closes #9758

pydata/xarray.title: Fix groupby median on dask arrays with non-contiguous groups
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

Since #11239, `groupby(...).median()` on dask arrays uses flox with `method="blockwise"`. flox can only rechunk so that chunk boundaries line up with group boundaries if the members of each group are contiguous along the grouped dimension. With interleaved labels spread over multiple chunks (e.g. `['1', '2', '1', '2']` with `chunks=1`), each block returns the same group again and flox fails with `InvalidIndexError: Reindexing only valid with uniquely valued Index objects`.

This PR shuffles the object (and the grouper codes) with `dask.array.shuffle` before calling flox, whenever `method="blockwise"` is used, the grouped dimension has multiple chunks, and the groups are not contiguous. This also fixes the same failure for other reductions when users pass `method="blockwise"` explicitly. Contiguous groups (e.g. resample) are unchanged and still handled by flox's rechunking. Grouping by multi-dimensional or chunked arrays is not affected by this change.

Once xarray-contrib/flox#501 is fixed, flox would shuffle on its own; the shuffle here stays correct (flox finds nothing left to do) and can then be restricted to older flox versions. There's a TODO in the code for that.

pydata/xarray.title: Hold the netCDF-C lock while accessing netCDF4 metadata
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

netCDF-C is not thread-safe, but the netCDF4 backend only held its lock while opening a file. Everything after that ran without the lock, in `open_dataset` and in `to_netcdf`. That includes reading variables, attributes, `data_model` and `filepath()`, and writing dimensions, variables and attributes, plus `sync()`. As a result, opening or writing netCDF4 files from several threads fails with `NetCDF: HDF error`, or crashes the process with segfaults and double frees. This is the "missing lock" discussed in #9779 and #7079.

### Changes

- **Reentrant locks.** Metadata access acquires the store's lock again internally, e.g. through `self.ds` and the array wrappers, so holding the lock around it requires a reentrant lock.
  - `SerializableLock` gets an opt-in `reentrant=True`. It is backed by a small reentrant lock that also supports `locked()` on Python < 3.14, where `RLock.locked()` does not exist. The reentrant flag is included in the pickled state.
  - The global `HDF5_LOCK` and `NETCDFC_LOCK` are reentrant, and so are the per-file write locks for the threaded scheduler (`_get_threaded_lock`).
  - A new `is_reentrant_lock()` helper checks for this, including for `CombinedLock`.
- **netCDF4 reads.** The store holds its lock while reading metadata:
  - in its constructor
  - for the whole `open_dataset` call
  - during the group walk in `open_groups_as_dict`
- **netCDF4 writes.** The store holds its lock in `set_attributes`, `set_dimensions`, `set_variables` and `sync()`. Encoding still runs outside the lock on purpose: it can compute dask arrays whose tasks need the same lock, so holding it there could deadlock.
- **Distributed.** The global `HDF5_LOCK` and `NETCDFC_LOCK` used to get a random token in every process. A dataset opened on one dask distributed worker and read on another therefore unpickled its locks as new, separate locks. Its reads were then not excluded from that worker's own netCDF4 calls, so workers still crashed or failed with `NetCDF: HDF error`. This was broken on `main` as well. The global locks now have fixed tokens, so they always unpickle to the global locks of the receiving process. This relies on #11622 sorting the locks of an unpickled `CombinedLock` again: otherwise a worker could acquire the same locks in the order of another process and deadlock.
- **Locks that are not reentrant are not held.** This covers user-supplied locks and the write locks of the distributed and multiprocessing schedulers, which come from other libraries. These behave as before, to avoid deadlocks. The `lock` descriptions of `open_dataset`, `open_dataarray`, `open_datatree` and `open_groups` now warn about custom locks.
- **Tests.**
  - `test_open_mfdataset_manyfiles` is fully un-skipped. It had been skipped since #8989 because it could crash the worker. #11622 fixed it except for its netcdf4 + `parallel=True` cases, which were still skipped.
  - New tests `test_netcdf4_concurrent_writes` and `test_netcdf4_concurrent_opens` run without dask. Both segfaulted in 3 of 3 runs without this change.
  - New tests `test_open_mfdataset_netcdf4_parallel` (threads) and `test_open_mfdataset_netcdf4_parallel_distributed` (a 2-worker cluster with 4 threads each) follow the MVCE in #11088. They take about 1 s and 2.5 s. Without this change, the threaded one failed 5 of 6 runs (segfault, double free or `HDF error`). The distributed one hung until the timeout in 3 of 4 runs and raised a `KeyError` in the fourth; with only the fixed lock tokens reverted, it hung in 4 of 4.
  - `test_open_mfdataset_multiple_files_parallel_distributed`, added in #7488 to reproduce #7079, now uses 4 threads per worker and opens the files 5 times. With the default single-threaded workers it never opened files concurrently within a process, which is why it never caught the bug. It takes about 2 s per case. Without this change, the `parallel=True` case failed 3 of 4 runs.
  - New lock tests cover reentrancy, blocking other threads, release from the wrong thread, the pickle round-trip, `is_reentrant_lock`, and unpickling the global locks in a spawned process.

### Verification

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| MVCE from #9779 (`dask.delayed` + `open_dataset`) | crashed 5/5 (double free or segfault) | 5/5 clean |
| MVCE from #9125 | 9/15 runs ok (`HDF error`, `KeyError`) | 15/15 ok |
| `open_mfdataset(parallel=True)`, 20 netCDF4 files | ~60% of attempts failed, one process crashed with a double free | 0/120 failed |
| 8 threads each writing its own file with `to_netcdf` | segfault 4/4 | 0/80 failed |
| jsignell's MVCE from #11088 (2 files, `parallel=True`) | crashed 2 of 10 processes (double free, segfault) | 10/10 clean |
| #11088-style with `decode_cf=False`, `preprocess`, 12 files, threads | crashed 4 of 5 processes | 5/5 clean |
| Same with a distributed cluster (2 workers × 4 threads) | `HDF error` and killed workers in every run | 75/75 opens ok |
| `test_open_mfdataset_manyfiles` | netcdf4 + `parallel=True` skipped | all 64 cases pass, 10/10 runs |

The full test suite passes locally with `--run-flaky`, including the distributed tests. mypy passes on py311 and py314.

### Note on #7079

I couldn't reproduce the exact error from #7079, `[Errno -51] NetCDF: Unknown file format`. With netCDF4 files and `parallel=True`, the unfixed code fails with `NetCDF: HDF error`, `Can't open HDF5 attribute`, segfaults and double frees instead. Nearly every process failed, including with a mix of netCDF3 and netCDF4 files and with 64 files on 16 threads. With this PR, all 280 opens in those runs succeeded. Pure netCDF3 files never failed, even without this change.

Everything else matches #7079:
- It started with netCDF4-python 1.6.1, which stopped serializing netCDF-C calls.
- It only happens with `parallel=True` and threads, and `scheduler="single-threaded"` avoids it.
- It succeeds on retry.

netCDF-C returns `-51` when it can't detect a file's format, and for netCDF4 files that detection goes through HDF5, the part the race corrupts. So the reporters' older netCDF-C/HDF5 builds likely report the same race as `-51`. Remote OPeNDAP files, mentioned later in #7079, are covered too, since they use `NETCDFC_LOCK`.

If anyone still sees `Unknown file format` with this change, please reopen #7079.

pydata/xarray.title: Raise error in diff() for a non-existent dimension
pydata/xarray.body:
## Description

### What is the issue?

Calling `.diff()` with a dimension that does not exist on the object, for example `da.diff("b")`, previously returned the object unchanged instead of raising an error.

This was inconsistent with related methods such as `mean` and `differentiate`, which already raise a `ValueError` when given an invalid dimension. This addresses issue #7748.

### What does this change do?

`Dataset.diff` now validates the requested dimension before the `n == 0` early return. This ensures that an invalid dimension raises the expected `ValueError` even when `n=0`.

`DataArray.diff` uses `Dataset.diff` internally, so the same validation also fixes the `DataArray` case. The error message follows the existing wording used elsewhere in the module.

### Design choice

I chose to raise the error directly rather than introduce a deprecation cycle.

The existing behavior appears to be an unintended silent result rather than a useful compatibility behavior: the issue is labeled as a bug, and related methods already raise `ValueError` for invalid dimensions. If a deprecation cycle is preferred, this can be changed to emit a `FutureWarning` first.

### Tests

Regression tests were added for both `DataArray` and `Dataset` to verify that an invalid dimension passed to `.diff()` raises the expected error.

This supersedes the abandoned PR #8962.

pydata/xarray.title: fix(indexing): align in-memory indexer for empty ndarray keys
pydata/xarray.body:
## What

`_decompose_outer_indexer()` in `xarray/core/indexing.py` turns an empty indexer array
into an empty slice `slice(0, 0)` for the backend, but the in-memory (`np_indexer`) half
of the decomposed key did not get a matching entry, and the `BASIC` branch had no
empty-array handling at all.

An empty slice **keeps** the dimension, unlike an integer key (which genuinely drops it
and correctly gets no `np_indexer` entry). So the returned `np_indexer` tuple ended up one
element shorter than the number of axes of the array the backend loaded, and applying it
indexed the wrong axes.

The fix makes one rule uniform across every `IndexingSupport` level: **a backend never
receives an empty index array** — it is always converted to an empty slice, and the
in-memory indexer always gets a matching `slice(None)` entry (16 lines total):

```python
if isinstance(k, np.ndarray) and k.size == 0:
    # empty np.ndarray key is converted to empty slice
    backend_indexer.append(slice(0, 0))
    np_indexer.append(slice(None))
```

## Why, and what it fixes per engine

The empty-array special case was added in #10870 for the 1-D case reported in #10867. It
was only added to the `OUTER_1VECTOR` branch, it omitted the in-memory indexer entry, and
the `BASIC` and `OUTER` branches were left untouched. All of it is invisible for 1-D
variables, where the resulting `np_indexer` is an empty tuple that
`explicit_indexing_adapter` skips — which is why the existing `test_empty_isel` regression
test (a 1-D variable) did not catch any of this.

| `IndexingSupport` | engines | symptom on `main` for a multi-dimensional variable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OUTER_1VECTOR` | h5netcdf, scipy | `IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0` (#11625) |
| `OUTER` | netCDF4 | **silently returns a wrongly-sized array** — see below |
| `BASIC` | pydap | `ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity` (#9075) |
| `VECTORIZED` | zarr | unaffected (does not take this path) |

The netCDF4 case is the nastiest one and is what motivated applying the same rule to
`OUTER` as well. `netCDF4` returns a mis-shaped array when it is handed an empty index
array in an outer key, and `OUTER` was passing the empty array straight through:

```
var[(array([], dtype=int64), array([0, 2]))]  ->  (0, 1)   # want (0, 2)
var[(array([1, 3]), array([], dtype=int64))]  ->  (1, 0)   # want (2, 0)
var[(slice(0, 0),     array([0, 2]))]         ->  (0, 2)   # correct
var[(array([1, 3]),   slice(0, 0))]           ->  (2, 0)   # correct
```

An empty *slice* is handled correctly by every backend, which is why converting to a slice
is the robust fix rather than patching the in-memory half alone.

Enumerating every combination of `{empty array, integer array, slice}` per axis and
comparing `decompose_indexer()` against direct outer indexing, before → after:

| `IndexingSupport` | 2-D `(4, 5)` | 3-D `(4, 5, 6)` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OUTER` | 9/9 → 9/9 | 27/27 → 27/27 |
| `OUTER_1VECTOR` | 8/9 → **9/9** | 20/27 → **27/27** |
| `BASIC` | 4/9 → **9/9** | 8/27 → **27/27** |

## Reproduction

```python
import numpy as np

import xarray as xr

path = "repro.nc"

in_memory = xr.Dataset(
    {"v": (("x", "y"), np.arange(20.0).reshape(4, 5))},
    coords={"x": np.arange(4), "y": np.arange(5)},
)
in_memory.to_netcdf(path, engine="scipy")   # or engine="netcdf4"

on_disk = xr.open_dataset(path, engine="scipy")

print(in_memory.isel(x=[], y=[1, 3])["v"].shape)  # (0, 2)
print(on_disk.isel(x=[], y=[1, 3])["v"].shape)    # IndexError on main
```

With `engine="scipy"` / `engine="h5netcdf"`, `main` raises:

```
File ".../xarray/backends/scipy_.py", line 97, in __getitem__
  data = indexing.explicit_indexing_adapter(
File ".../xarray/core/indexing.py", line 1166, in explicit_indexing_adapter
  result = apply_indexer(indexable, numpy_indices)
File ".../xarray/core/indexing.py", line 1707, in _oindex_get
  return self.array[key]
IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0
```

With `engine="netcdf4"`, `main` does not raise but the loaded array has shape `(0, 1)`
whereas xarray reports `(0, 2)`, so `assert_identical` fails. Either way the expected
result is `(0, 2)`, matching the in-memory operation.

## How this was tested

`test_indexing.py` gains `test_decompose_indexer_empty_ndarray`, parameterized over
shapes, the position of the empty axis, and all four `IndexingSupport` levels.
`test_backends.py` gains `test_empty_isel_multidim` in `DatasetIOBase`, so every engine
round-trips a 2-D variable through an empty indexer (inherited by the datatree backend
tests as well).

```
$ python -m pytest xarray/tests/test_indexing.py -q
171 passed, 6 skipped in 7.09s

$ python -m pytest xarray/tests/test_backends.py -k empty_isel
14 passed, 20 skipped in 32.37s

$ python -m pytest xarray/tests/test_backends.py -q -n 4
2 failed, 664 passed, 1731 skipped, 21 xfailed, 7 xpassed

$ python -m pytest xarray/tests/test_variable.py xarray/tests/test_backends_datatree.py -q -n 4
524 passed, 311 skipped, 8 xfailed, 3 xpassed
```

The new tests fail without the fix. With `xarray/core/indexing.py` reverted to
`upstream/main` and the tests left in place:

```
$ python -m pytest xarray/tests/test_indexing.py -q -k empty_ndarray
7 failed, 9 passed, 161 deselected
    # 4x IndexingSupport.BASIC  -> ValueError: zero-size array to reduction
    # 3x IndexingSupport.OUTER_1VECTOR -> IndexError / ValueError: zip() argument 2 is longer

$ python -m pytest xarray/tests/test_backends.py xarray/tests/test_backends_datatree.py -q -k empty_isel
8 failed, 8 passed, 20 skipped
    # all 8 failures are test_empty_isel_multidim:
    #   TestNetCDF4Data, TestNetCDF3ViaNetCDF4Data, TestNetCDF4ClassicViaNetCDF4Data,
    #   TestGenericNetCDFData, TestNetCDF4DataTree,
    #   TestScipyInMemoryData, TestScipyFileObject, TestScipyFilePath
```

The pre-existing 1-D `test_empty_isel` passes both with and without the fix, which is
precisely why it did not catch this.

### Pre-existing local failures (not caused by this PR)

- `test_backends.py::test_write_file_from_np_str[str]` and `[str_]`, and 9 failures in
  `test_dataset.py` (`test_repr`, `test_sel_categorical*`, `test_categorical_multiindex`,
  `test_from_dataframe_categorical_*`, `test_fillna/dropna_extension_array`). All are
  artifacts of the local environment and were verified to fail identically on unmodified
  `upstream/main`: 8-9 of them are
  `ImportError: Pandas requires version '2024.10.0' or newer of 'xarray' (version '0.0.0')`
  raised by pandas' optional-dependency version gate against the editable install (which
  has no version tag because the clone is a blobless partial clone), and `test_repr` is a
  categorical `32B` vs `36B` repr difference from pandas 3.0.6.

Fixes #11625
Fixes #9075

pydata/xarray.title: Forbid forward slashes in DataTree child names
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

Assigning `DataTree` children under a name containing `/` currently recurses until `RecursionError` instead of raising a clear error:

```python
xr.DataTree(children={"a/b": xr.DataTree()})  # RecursionError
```

Two things combine to cause this:

1. The name was only validated in `NamedNode._post_attach`, i.e. *after* the child had already been inserted into the parent's `_children` dict.
2. The rollback in the `children` setter re-assigned `old_children`, which was a `Frozen` **view** of that same dict rather than a copy. When the parent had no prior children, `_detach` never swapped the dict out, so the view now contained the bad child and each rollback re-triggered the same error.

This PR:
- validates child names up front in `TreeNode._check_children` (reusing `_validate_name`), as suggested in the issue, so nothing is mutated on bad input;
- snapshots `old_children` with `dict(...)` so the rollback is correct for any failure during attach.

Path-style assignment via `tree["a/b"] = ...` and `DataTree.from_dict({"a/b": ...})` is unaffected; those intentionally interpret `/` as a path.

pydata/xarray.title: Fix the last-release benchmark workflow running zero benchmarks
pydata/xarray.body:
Closes #11533

The `Benchmark compare last release` workflow has been finishing green in ~30s without running a single benchmark.

`asv_bench/asv.conf.json` moved to `"environment_type": "rattler"` in #10866, and `py-rattler` was added to `ci/requirements/environment-benchmark.yml`. This workflow builds its environment from `ci/requirements/environment.yml`, which never got `py-rattler`, so asv exits with:

```
· Unknown environment type 'rattler'. Allowed values based on existing plugins are ['existing', 'conda', 'uv', 'virtualenv'].
· No environments selected
```

That failure is invisible because the run step pipes `asv continuous ... | sed ... | tee benchmarks.log` without `pipefail`, and the only gate is a grep for `Traceback \|failed\|PERFORMANCE DECREASED`, which an environment-construction failure never matches.

This switches the workflow to `environment-benchmark.yml` (matching `benchmarks.yml`), renames the environment accordingly, adds `python-build` to `create-args` as `benchmarks.yml` already does, and sets `pipefail` so a failing asv run fails the job instead of being swallowed by `tee`.

pydata/xarray.title: Fix type error for Coarsen reduction methods
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description
The methods for the documented reduction operations on `Dataset.coarsen()` and `DataArray.coarsen()` were dynamically generated via injected methods that relied on code in several different modules. The dynamic generation of these methods also meant that type errors were raised when trying to access reduction methods, e.g., the following code example.

<details>
  <summary>Minimal working example</summary>

  ```python
  import numpy as np
  import xarray as xr
  
  rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
  data = rng.random((10, 10))
  
  ds = xr.Dataset(
      {
          "z": (("x", "y"), data)
      },
      coords={
          "x": np.arange(10),
          "y": np.arange(10)
      },
  )

  # raises Object of type `DatasetCoarsen` has no attribute `mean` ty[unresolved-attribute]
  ds_coarsen = ds.coarsen(x=2).mean() 
  ```
</details>

This PR moves all the logic for `Coarsen` into `xarray.computation.rolling` and attempts to mirror the implementation of `xarray.computation.rolling.Rolling`. It should result in no functional changes as far as I can tell and should make future maintenance slightly easier (not having to track the injection across files).

Closes #9789

## Problem

`apply_ufunc` currently treats `DataTree` as a dict-like object. Unary calls silently return only the root `Dataset`, while core-dimension and multi-tree calls can fail when child nodes reach the variable dispatch path.

pydata/xarray.title: Fix idxmax/idxmin silently promoting integer label coordinate dtype to float64 (GH#7527)
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

`DataArray.idxmax`/`idxmin` (and the `Dataset` equivalents) silently promoted the dtype of the returned *label* coordinate to `float64` whenever the input data was floating-point — even when the reduced dimension's coordinate was an integer (e.g. `int64`). This is GH#7527, open since 2023 with no fix.

Root cause: in `xarray/computation/computation.py::_calc_idxminmax`, the `res.where(~allna, fill_value)` step ran unconditionally for every floating-point input. Calling `.where` with the default float `fill_value` cast the integer label coordinate to float, even for fully-valid reduction slices that never needed filling.

Fix: only call `.where` when at least one slice is actually all-`NaN` (`allna.any()`). Fully-valid slices keep their original coordinate dtype; all-`NaN` slices still get the float `fill_value` as before.

pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

Fixes #6891.

`Dataset.curvefit` and `DataArray.curvefit` both document their scipy passthrough as
`**kwargs : optional`, so calling them the way the docstring describes fails:

```python
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

def exp(t, a, b):
    return a * np.exp(b * t)

t = np.linspace(0, 1, 20)
da = xr.DataArray(exp(t, 2.0, -1.0), dims="t", coords={"t": t})
da.curvefit("t", exp, method="trf")
```

```
TypeError: DataArray.curvefit() got an unexpected keyword argument 'method'
```

Same on `Dataset`. Neither method actually has a `VAR_KEYWORD` parameter, they take a single `kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None`, and `kwargs={"method": "trf"}` works fine. So the docstrings are wrong, not the behaviour. [`computation/fit.py`](https://github.com/pydata/xarray/blob/abdc46498ddaf623e057c18ce35799be865bed54/xarray/computation/fit.py#L371),
which both methods delegate to, already documents the parameter correctly, the class docstrings
just drifted from it in #5182. headtr1ck
[scoped this fix on the issue](https://github.com/pydata/xarray/issues/6891#issuecomment-1484199176):
change `**kwargs` to `kwargs` in both docstrings.

pydata/xarray.title: Fix alignment and copy of transposed CoordinateTransformIndex-backed arrays
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

Fixes two bugs affecting `CoordinateTransformIndex`-backed coordinates after `.transpose()`:

- `Aligner.align_indexes` (`xarray/structure/alignment.py`) grouped indexes for comparison by `(coordinate name, dims order)` before ever calling `Index.equals()`. Two objects sharing an equal multi-dimensional index but differing only in the dims order of their coordinate variables (e.g. one was transposed) landed in different groups and raised a spurious `AlignmentError: conflicting indexes`, even though the indexes were genuinely equal. Now defers to `Index.equals()` (via `indexes_all_equal`, with its existing `NotImplementedError` fallback to variable comparison) before treating a coordinate-name collision across groups as a real conflict.
- `CoordinateTransformIndex.create_variables()` (`xarray/core/indexes.py`) always rebuilt coordinate variables with `Variable(self.transform.dims, ...)` (the transform's *original* dims order) discarding any prior `.transpose()`. Since `Variable.transpose()` never mutates the underlying transform, this silently reverted the transpose on `.copy()`, `copy.deepcopy()`, and the `join="exact"` fast path in `xr.align()`, leaving the array's data and coordinate dims orders inconsistent. Now preserves the incoming variable's dims order when it's a permutation of the transform's own.

pydata/xarray.title: Don't warn about a missing _FillValue for CF coordinate variables
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

Closes #10305.

When a float variable is encoded to an integer dtype, `NonStringCoder.encode` warns that there is no `_FillValue` to use for NaNs. That warning also fired for CF coordinate variables, meaning 1D variables named after their own dimension. CF says missing data is not allowed in coordinate variables, so those variables are not supposed to carry a `_FillValue` at all. The warning pushed people toward adding one, which a CF checker then flags.

The fix skips the warning when a variable's dims are exactly `(name,)`, which is the check @kmuehlbauer suggested on the issue. Rounding and the dtype cast are left alone, so the encoded output is the same as before. Data variables and multidimensional auxiliary coordinates still warn, and there are tests for both cases.

This covers only the first part of the issue. The other part, what to do when someone sets `_FillValue = None` and the float data really does contain NaN, is left out on purpose. @kmuehlbauer noted that the cast result there depends on the platform, so it seems better to handle it separately.

pydata/xarray.title: Raise a TypeError when a Coordinates object is used as a coordinate value
pydata/xarray.body:
### Description

Passing a `Coordinates` object as a value inside a coords mapping, like `ds.assign_coords({"x": coords})`, was never caught. It fell through `as_variable` into `as_compatible_data`, which treats the mapping as a sequence and builds an array out of its coordinate names. If the number of names happened to match the dimension size you got no error at all, just a coordinate holding the names. Otherwise you got a "conflicting sizes for dimension" error further down that gives no hint about what actually went wrong.

`as_variable` now checks for a `Coordinates` object and raises a `TypeError` telling you to pass it directly with `ds.assign_coords(coords)`. Doing the check there covers `assign_coords` on both `Dataset` and `DataArray` and both constructors in one place.

One existing test, `test_drop_attrs`, built its multi-index through the broken spelling, so its `z` coordinate was really a `<U1` array of coordinate names rather than a multi-index. It now passes the `Coordinates` object directly.
