pydata/xarray.title: Require to explicitly defining optional dimensions such as hue and markersize
pydata/xarray.body:
- [x] Closes #7314
- [x] Closes #7268

* Matplotlib adds default colors with `plt.plot(x, y)` when `y` is a 2D array.
* Matplotlib prioritizes `c` over default colors with `plt.plot(x, y, c="blue")` when `y` is a 2D array.
* Seaborn prioritizes `hue` over `c`, but all plot axes has to be explicit.

The plot1d function now follows closer to seaborns example and require explicitly defining optional dimensions such as  hue/markersize. Positives and negatives:
+++ Reliable performance, won't accidentally choose large and heavy arrays to plot.
\- Loss of dimension information for default values, will essentially flatten the n-dimensional arrays.
\- Other xarray plot functions guesses quite a bit as well, API is not consistent.

Required dimensions like the x-axis will still be guessed since the mpl errors weren't very intuitive.

While at it:
* Make it possible to prioritize certain mpl kwargs when hue/markersize isn't defined.
* Fix integer coords in `plot1`d and facetgrid, use `.coords` instead of `getitem`.

pydata/xarray.title: Save groupby codes after factorizing, pass to flox
pydata/xarray.body:
<!-- Feel free to remove check-list items aren't relevant to your change -->

- [x] Closes #6689,
- xref #6610
- [x] Closes #7601 
- [x] Tests added

This is an alternative to #6689. 
- There I tried to avoid factorizing in the GroupBy constructor, and passed the `by` variable directly to `flox`. Most GroupBy methods however depend on various steps in `__init__`, so it became messy.
- Here I instead preserve factorizing in the constructor and pass the factorized codes to `flox`. This simplifies things a lot. Since we'll want to preserve the "for loop over groups" approach for `GroupBy.map`, we'll need something like this anyway.
 
The large amount of deleted code in `_flox_reduce` here suggests to me that this is the better approach.

I think we could also use this to generalize to multiple groupers:
- factorize each,
- `ravel_muti_index` to generate a singe variable to groupby
- apply
- reshape to output shape
- assign new indices.

NCAR/geocat-comp.title: heat_index warnings and bug
Adapt climatology functions to allow for monthly input data with centered time stamps
NCAR/geocat-comp.body:
## PR Summary
Adapts `climate_anomaly` and `climatology_average` to allow for monthly input data with more flexibility regarding time specification, updates docs, and adds test coverage.

Previously, we only allowed input data that where we could use Xarray's `infer_freq` to determine the input data frequency and ensure uniform spacing in the time dimension.  This prevented the functions from working with some CESM data where the monthly data has a mid-month time coordinate and therefore the temporal frequency can't be directly inferred. 

While some uniformity is still necessary to support internal functions such as `_calculate_center_of_time_bounds`, the requirement to have month start or month end dates in order to infer a monthly frequency was overly restrictive.  This PR allows for exceptions to the uniform spacing requirement for monthly data.  

## Related Tickets & Documents
Closes #676

NCAR/geocat-comp.title: Initial benchmarks
NCAR/geocat-comp.body: ## PR Summary This PR creates an initial set of benchmarks for `geocat-comp` ### Design notes: - These benchmarks are based on our testing suite and are designed to be a starting point to which we can add more specific tests to in the future. - I have purposely not included large benchmarks in this initial suite, as I do not want to significantly increase the benchmark CI run time and it's outside of this PR's scope to come up with a way to create/store larger datasets. - Following from this, I also did not add any dask specific benchmarks, because small runs aren't the best use case for dask and I did not want to deal with handling spinning up/shutting down a lot of dask clusters while not having any large tests. - I aimed to test a representative subset of our functions and only left out functions I thought were reasonably computationally the same or called by other functions' benchmarks. I recognize that this could be subjective and I did also try to limit the number of benchmarks where I thought I could, feel free to disagree with what I left out (or included) - I included `peakmem` tests where I know there have been memory considerations previously. I did not write any `mem` benchmarks because I did not see any clear places where memory as opposed to peakmem would provide any more of a warning when weighed against the increase in run time that adding `mem` tests would add, especially since this initial suite does not include larger tests. I am also completely open to feedback on this design choice. ### Changes - 34 new benchmarks (35 total) organized into different files corresponding to module that (aim to) cover a representative subset of geocat-comp's functionality - changed run range in `asv-benchmarking.yml` `v2024.04.0..main` -> `v2025.10.1..main` to avoid running the new benchmarks over all commits to main since `v2024.04.0`. This will not affect the current stored benchmark results - adds `geocat.datafiles` to `build_envs/asv-bench.yml` ### CI performance impacts As this is right now, believe that regular ASV runs on main would run 75 benchmarks (1 commit, 2 env, 35 bench) and PR comparison runs would run 140 benchmarks (2 commits, 2 env, 35 bench), which still gives reasonable CI run times: After - 75 total benchmarks (2 commits * **1 environments** * 35 benchmarks) -> [8m 30s](https://github.com/NCAR/geocat-comp/actions/runs/18365468242/job/52317837486?pr=772) - 140 total benchmarks (2 commits * **2 environments** * 35 benchmarks) -> [15m 23s](https://github.com/NCAR/geocat-comp/actions/runs/18383167015/job/52374773640?pr=772) Before - 4 total benchmarks (2 commits * 2 environments * 1 benchmarks) -> [6m 7s](https://github.com/NCAR/geocat-comp/actions/runs/18365468242/job/52317837486?pr=772) ### Preview of updated ASV benchmark suite from local runs ## Future improvement ideas - restrict PR comparison runs to use only one python version for comparison, halving the benchmarks run - pull latest benchmarking results from asv repo, removing the need to run benchmarks for main if they exist already - some sort of filtering to only run the benchmarks relevant to the files changed in a given PR - consider running PR comparison benchmarks w/ `--quick`, or at least provide it as an option (from asv docs:) > Do a "quick" run, where each benchmark function is run only once. This is useful to find basic errors in the benchmark functions faster. The results are unlikely to be useful, and thus are not saved - put the ASV PR comment comparison table into a collapsible section or something to reduce length of comment - find a way to handle larger and dask-specific benchmarks ## Related Tickets & Documents Closes #469 ## PR Checklist **General** - [x] PR includes a summary of changes - [x] Link relevant issues, make one if none exist - [x] Add a brief summary of changes to `docs/release-notes.rst` in a relevant section for the upcoming release. - [x] Add appropriate labels to this PR - [x] PR follows the [Contributor's Guide](https://geocat-comp.readthedocs.io/en/stable/contrib.html)

NCAR/geocat-comp.body:
## PR Summary
This PR addresses permission errors with the original `asv-pr.yml` by splitting the workflow into two pieces, `asv-pr-commenter.yml` and `run-asv-pr.yml` as described in this GitHub Security Lab post[
](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/) and suggested by @kafitzgerald.

See both sides of the split workflow [working on my fork](https://github.com/anissa111/geocat-comp/pull/24). I don't have a way to test this on a fully forked workflow, but I anticipate this working because the commenting portion of the workflow should work the same (through PR number from base repo) for forks and branches.

~This PR changes `asv-pr.yml` to run on `pull_request_target` instead of `pull_request`.~

~I do not have a way to test this (github can't handle forks of forks), but I believe this will solve the issue. See [this explanation](https://github.com/thollander/actions-comment-pull-request#permissions) on a workflow that performs a similar functionality:~

~I expect the asv run to fail on this PR, but I had to give it a shot to make sure. edit: ah yeah never mind it didn't run, which I think also makes sense because the version on main is expecting the workflow to run from the forked branch and this branch is expecting it to be run from the upstream.~

NCAR/geocat-comp.title: Change `interp_hybrid_to_pressure` temperature extrapolation to use `t_bot` directly
NCAR/geocat-comp.body:
## PR Summary
Changes the `interp_hybrid_to_pressure` temperature extrapolation to use `t_bot` directly rather than using the presumed lower level of the input temperature data which relies upon the vertical coordinate being indexed in a certain direction.

The prior behavior was, as far as I can tell, inherited from NCL.  However, the assumption this relies upon was [documented there](https://www.ncl.ucar.edu/Document/Functions/Built-in/vinth2p_ecmwf.shtml) whereas we failed to do so or test for it in GeoCAT-comp.

Interestingly, we required an input for `t_bot` in GeoCAT-comp when extrapolation is set to `True`, but ignored it for the temperature extrapolation previously (likely also inherited behavior from NCL).  Leveraging `t_bot` directly avoids the issue with indexing and gives more control to the user to define the temperature field they would like to use.  However, it does change the answers in some cases.  For example, in the relevant test we assign `t_bot` as the surface temperature field, which is slightly different from the lowest temperature level and therefore results in a different answer.  I adjusted the specification of `t_bot` there for consistency with the NCL results.

Based upon the GeoCAT-comp documentation, this new behavior is what I would have expected the whole time so I think it makes sense to treat this as a bug fix.  It'd be great to get other's perspective on this though.

Closes #735

NCAR/geocat-comp.title: Support updates
NCAR/geocat-comp.body:
## PR Summary

The motivation for this PR was to remove the reference to the old ncar/geocat repo as a suggested support mechanism.  I opted to do that by adjusting the language and recommendations on our longer format support page.  This allows us to keep that additional content, but isn't consistent with the simplified approach used in geocat-applications or geocat-examples that just links out to GitHub issues and the GeoCAT suggestion box.  I'm inclined to keep at least viz and comp consistent, but don't have too strong of an opinion otherwise.  Curious what others think.

Currently, this PR does the following:
* Removes reference to ncar/geocat repo from support page
* Minor updates to support page language
* Changes "feature request form" to "suggestion box" for consistency

## Related Tickets & Documents
Closes #706

NCAR/geocat-comp.title: Minimum dependency version testing and backwards compatibility
NCAR/geocat-comp.body:
## PR Summary
Adds a minimum dependency environment file and testing to CI and makes a few minor changes for backwards compatibility with earlier versions of Pandas and Xarray to climatology functions and associated testing.  I thought about separating those out into their own PR, but the changes are quite minor.

What's missing:
* documentation for users + devs
* minimum versions in our dependency specification

I'm open to adding these now, but wonder if it might make sense to hold off a bit in case we opt to make changes (e.g. include other packages, change versions, etc.).  Also, I'm not aware of specific limitations to our backward compatibility so these would just be the limits of what we're testing.

## Related Tickets & Documents
Closes #697

NCAR/geocat-comp.title: Update scipy and use `sph_harm_y`
NCAR/geocat-comp.body:
## PR Summary

This PR broadly:
- unpins scipy
- updates `sph_harm` to new `sph_harm_y`

To update from `sph_harm` to `sph_harm_y`:
- swaps input order of `m` and `n`
- flips `phi` and `theta` before passing to `sph_harm_y` to maintain our current API instead of making a breaking change
- fixes several new array broadcasting issues
- adds some branching to ensure backwards compatibility with earlier scipy versions

It also:
- standardizes the scipy import in `spherical.py`
- removes internal rechunking in `decomposition()` and `recomposition`
- slightly improves input type checking in `decomposition()` and `recomposition` by doing a single `in_type = type(data)` instead of rechecking several times
- slightly reorganizes some of the dimensionality type handling for clarity
- makes several minor formatting changes
- changes the spherical tests to reuse the input test data generation with a pytest fixture
- standardizes internal and preserves user-defined xarray dimension names

There is still some clean up that could be done on these functions and the tests, but in order to maintain some scope, I've tried to limit the miscellaneous improvements to just what helped clarify/debug the core issues addressed in the PR. I also tried to stay away from type handling improvements more than was strictly necessary, as I think those should be handled as part of the larger type handling improvements we're working on.

## Related Tickets & Documents
Closes #673

NCAR/geocat-comp.title: Python 3.13 support and testing
NCAR/geocat-comp.body:
## PR Summary
Bumps Python version pins to allow for Python 3.13 installs and adds Python 3.13 to testing.

Notably this doesn't bump Python versions for things like ASV and Codecov - not sure if we want to do that now as well.  

It also does not drop support for Python 3.10.  This means our testing matrix will get larger.  If that's an issue, we might think about testing min / max versions or at least not all versions on all platforms.  Dropping support for 3.10 right now seems a little soon.

## Related Tickets & Documents
Closes #675

Also, moves up the earliest tag to start benchmarking since commits before `v2023.02.0` fail on import

See on my fork for tag `v2022.10.0`, which we know will fail from [these logs](https://github.com/NCAR/geocat-comp/actions/runs/6699414577/job/18203492348)

NCAR/geocat-comp.title: Connect ASV benchmarking to CI
NCAR/geocat-comp.body:
## PR Summary
<!-- Summary goes here. Replace XXX with the number of the issue this PR will resolve. -->
Closes #472

To see this in action, see my [fork](https://github.com/anissa111/geocat-comp/commit/65b8ba280fcc0f402dbedcc6c8fd7ac5c8af16f2).
- Benchmarks run in [this action](https://github.com/anissa111/geocat-comp/actions/runs/6669934123/job/18128763915), producing [this commit](https://github.com/NCAR/geocat-comp-asv/commit/5dc6738e494c3594f06eb437daac6630e69fdc61) on NCAR/geocat-asv
- Then, I manually re-run the benchmarks in [this action](https://github.com/anissa111/geocat-comp/actions/runs/6670020074). It does not re-run the previously run benchmarks in the previous actions, and [fails here](https://github.com/anissa111/geocat-comp/actions/runs/6670020074/job/18129048254#step:8:1) on purpose.

In this PR, I made a couple changes from the proof of concept runs above:
- I've increased the number of commits that gets benchmarked. For our actual CI, I've set it to benchmark all commits from the `v2022.10.0` tag forward. This will take a while to run the first time, but should only produce long CI runs when a new benchmark is added in the future.
- I've altered the last step, the push to NCAR/geocat-comp-asv, to only run if the CI is coming from this repository from the main branch. This addition is to make sure that any manual runs on branches other than main do not get included in our archived benchmark results.

Here are a couple of design decisions that might warrant further discussion:
- the action will fail if there are no new benchmarks to be committed. I thought about putting some checks to make sure the action passed anyway, but decided against it. If this CI, which runs automatically on pushes to main and tagged versions, can't find a new push to main or tagged version to benchmark (or fails to produce benchmarks), I assume we might actually want that failure to notify us if something has gone weird. @kafitzgerald, what do you think here?
- How long do we actually want to produce a commit history for? Is `v2022.10.0` too long or too short?
- With this change, we'll really want to make sure to have clean commit histories before pushing to main, should we add any additional guard rails up for that?
- Just noting again that it feels really un-ideal to have my personal info added to authenticate the pushes, but I'm unsure how to get around that without fine-grained tokens and/or a bot

pytroll/pyresample.title: Densify the geostationary bounding polygon before reprojecting in AreaSlicer
pytroll/pyresample.body:
`AreaSlicer.get_polygon_to_contain` builds the bounding polygon of a geostationary source disk and reprojects it into the destination projection to compute the source slice. When the source is a partial disk (rapid scan or region of interest data), clipping the disk to its area extent introduces straight chord edges with only two vertices. Those chords are not straight in the destination projection, so the reprojected polygon cuts the corner and the source slice comes out too small, leaving part of the destination empty. A full disk source is unaffected, because its whole boundary is the densely sampled disk arc.

This densifies the polygon with `segmentize` before reprojecting it, so the chord edges keep enough vertices to follow their true shape in the destination projection. The problem was found in satpy when resampling MSG rapid scan data to a polar stereographic area with `gradient_search`.

`segmentize` needs shapely 2.0 or newer. shapely is currently unpinned in the dependencies, so a `shapely>=2.0` pin can be added if you want it explicit.

pytroll/pyresample.title: Fix EWA ll2cr not handling non-C contiguous arrays
pytroll/pyresample.body:
CC @ameraner 

In #723 it was pointed out that non-C contiguous lon/lat inputs to the EWA ll2cr function are not handled. This PR fixes this by specifying the `order` kwarg to `astype` as well as using `numpy.require` to force write-ability on the inputs. I think this preserves the existing functionality while handling more use cases.

The main complication here is that old ll2cr has an optimization if some users want to use it where results are written in-place on the lon/lat inputs to avoid making extra arrays. This of course completely overwrites the lon/lat data in the arrays and is why the default is to copy the data, but I'd still like to support this behavior if it can be used in the future.

pytroll/pyresample.title: Fix AreaDefinition array index methods mishandling outer edge values
pytroll/pyresample.body:
An attempt to fix https://github.com/ssec/polar2grid/issues/691

Basically, current bounding operations via `get_area_slices` have trouble when the resulting lon/lat extents match *almost* exactly with the source area definition. This PR should fix a couple important bugs in the array index retrieval methods of the AreaDefinition:

1. Floating point precision issues where a X coordinate that is just outside the area (a float precision different) can still be considered part of the area (not masked).
2. Not including -0.5 to 0.0 pixel indexes as "0" (it is the left most part of the left most pixels.
3. Including an extra 0.5 pixels on the right of the area.

Locally I see one failure where my particular approach has changed the underlying value for elements that are masked and this test specifically checks that that doesn't happen (they stay unchanged).

I noticed while working on this that any unused kwarg is put into the future AreaDefinition's `.attrs` dictionary property. This is error prone as it means that any unrecognized property will go in as "metadata". I'd like to add an explicit `attrs:` section to the YAML for defining these metadata values.

pytroll/pyresample.title: Fix performance regression in base resampler class when comparing geometries
pytroll/pyresample.body:
As mentioned in #517, the new comparison added to the base resampler class in #508 was significantly slowing down any cases where non-areas were involved. This was most noticeable with EWA resampling as it is based on this resampler class and only deals with swath definitions.

The primary issue is/was that if the swaths are *not* equal the `==` used in the `if` statement was comparing the every coordinate (every pixel) of the source swath arrays to every pixel of the area definitions generated coordinates. This is usually not necessary since when we get to that point the objects are probably not equal and two swaths that aren't the same exact objects (or the underlying arrays are not the same) are probably not equal even if they have the same shape.

This PR is the first step in a proper fix. This should be released in a 1.27.1 release to fix the performance issue. The second step will be a separate PR (as discussed on the pytroll slack) where a `coordinates_equal` method will be added to the geometries to compare coordinates values no matter the cost in performance. The `__eq__` method will be updated to be strict about objects needing to be the same type and then take the shortcuts implemented in this PR.

ecmwf/cfgrib.title: Fix issue with alternativeRowScanning and mercator grid (#358)
ecmwf/cfgrib.body: Attempt to fix #358 - the problem occurs because the code to handle alternativeRowScanning assumed that the grid was regular lat/lon and therefor had 2 dimensions. The current case is a Mercator grid, represented with just 1 dimension and therefore does not need to handle alternativeRowScanning.

ecmwf/cfgrib.title: Renamed 'grib_errors' parameter to 'errors' to match open_file() signature
ecmwf/cfgrib.body:
Closes #348

Fixes a bug where providing `"grib_errors"` as key in backend_kwargs is required by some function (`open_variable_datasets()`) but causes a TypeError due to not being a recognized parameter in others (`CfGribBackend.open_dataset()`).

Also fixes a test (`test_40_xarray_store.py::test_open_dataset_corrupted()`) to specifically expect the type of Error associated with the expected issue, which was masking the TypeError.

Additionally, also adds the following line to `test_40_xarray_store.py::test_open_dataset()`:
`xarray_store.open_dataset(TEST_DATA, backend_kwargs={"errors": "raise"})`
This tests that calling `open_dataset()` with a known-good GRIB file and `"errors": "raise"` does not, in fact, raise an Error.

ecmwf/cfgrib.title: Prevent merging of different variables with the same name and date but different attributes
ecmwf/cfgrib.body:
closes #336

Fixes a bug where cfgrib would incorrectly combine two different variables if they happened to have the same shortName and data. For example, all-zeroes data GRIB messages with `stepType='instant'` and `stepType='avg'` attributes for `csrwe` (Convective snowfall rate water equivalent) on days without snow.
